words.exampleIeltsEn: Teachers who share their passion for science can inspire students to pursue careers in research.

words.definitionEn: A conversation, especially between characters in a story or play.
words.exampleDailyEn: The actors practised their dialog before stepping onto the stage.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Open dialog between local authorities and residents can help resolve disagreements about new housing developments.

words.definitionEn: a structure with triangular sides meeting at a point
words.exampleDailyEn: We built a small pyramid out of wooden blocks.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The management pyramid in many organisations places a small group of executives above numerous employees.

words.definitionEn: The official who leads or represents a city or town
words.exampleDailyEn: The mayor opened our new swimming pool yesterday.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The newly elected mayor has promised to improve public transport and create more affordable housing for residents.

words.definitionEn: material burned or used to produce heat or power
words.exampleDailyEn: We stopped for fuel before driving into the mountains.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Growing demand for private cars may fuel air pollution unless governments promote cleaner alternatives.

words.definitionEn: a competition involving several games between different players or teams
words.exampleDailyEn: Our school tennis tournament starts next Saturday morning.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Hosting an international tournament can boost tourism, but maintaining sports facilities afterwards may prove expensive.

words.definitionEn: An arrangement to reserve a room, seat, or service.
words.exampleDailyEn: I called the hotel to confirm our booking.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Online booking systems allow tourists to compare accommodation prices and plan their journeys more efficiently.

words.definitionEn: someone who pays for professional services
words.exampleDailyEn: The designer showed her client three possible kitchen layouts.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Maintaining clear communication with each client helps businesses build trust and establish lasting professional relationships.

words.definitionEn: words repeated exactly from another person or source
words.exampleDailyEn: She opened her speech with a quotation from a poem.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Before selecting a contractor, local authorities should obtain a detailed quotation for the proposed construction work.

words.definitionEn: An important subject or problem that needs discussion.
words.exampleDailyEn: We discussed the parking issue at our neighbourhood meeting.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Governments must address the issue of housing affordability to ensure that young adults can live independently.

words.definitionEn: At a time before now or before another event.
words.exampleDailyEn: I had previously met our neighbour at the library.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Online courses now provide educational opportunities for people who previously had limited access to universities.

words.definitionEn: a judgement formed after considering facts or evidence
words.exampleDailyEn: We reached the same conclusion after checking the receipts.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers should consider alternative explanations before drawing a conclusion from a relatively small sample.

words.definitionEn: Things produced for sale or transported for trade.
words.exampleDailyEn: The shop sells handmade goods from nearby villages.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Transporting goods by rail rather than road can lower emissions and reduce congestion in urban areas.

words.definitionEn: a device that stores computer data on a circular surface
words.exampleDailyEn: My laptop's disk is almost full of holiday photos.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular backups protect important research data against accidental deletion and unexpected disk failure in university computer systems.

words.definitionEn: a written account of someone's life by another person
words.exampleDailyEn: I'm reading a biography of an explorer before bed.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A well-researched biography can reveal how social conditions influence an individual's choices and achievements.

words.definitionEn: the smallest living unit of an organism
words.exampleDailyEn: Under the microscope, each onion cell looked like a rectangle.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Scientists study how damaged cells repair themselves to develop more effective treatments for disease.

words.definitionEn: a body temperature higher than normal, usually caused by illness
words.exampleDailyEn: He stayed in bed because he had a fever.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A persistent fever may indicate an infection and should be assessed by a qualified healthcare professional.

words.definitionEn: A room or floor below ground level in a building.
words.exampleDailyEn: We keep our bicycles in the basement during winter.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Converting unused basement space into community facilities can help densely populated neighbourhoods accommodate more activities.

words.definitionEn: not common or not happening often
words.exampleDailyEn: We spotted a rare bird beside the lake yesterday.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Protecting rare species requires long-term investment in habitat restoration and effective controls on illegal trade.

words.definitionEn: Sadness and concern for someone who is suffering.
words.exampleDailyEn: I felt pity for the puppy shivering in the rain.
words.exampleIeltsEn: It is a pity that many historic buildings are demolished before their cultural value is properly assessed.

words.definitionEn: The activity or business of promoting products and services.
words.exampleDailyEn: My sister works in advertising and designs colourful posters.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Advertising can influence consumer choices, which is why campaigns aimed at children require careful regulation.

words.definitionEn: A structure whose wind-driven sails power machinery, often for grinding grain.
words.exampleDailyEn: We watched the old windmill turn beside the river.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Restoring a traditional windmill can preserve local heritage while attracting visitors interested in the history of rural technology.

words.definitionEn: Someone whose work involves politics, especially an elected government member.
words.exampleDailyEn: A local politician visited our neighbourhood to discuss transport.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Politicians should consult local communities before making decisions that could affect access to public services.

words.definitionEn: a powerful tropical storm with extremely strong winds
words.exampleDailyEn: We stayed indoors as the hurricane approached the coast.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Coastal cities need stronger flood defences and reliable warning systems to protect residents when a hurricane approaches.

words.definitionEn: A person who competes in boxing.
words.exampleDailyEn: The boxer pulled on her gloves before training.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A professional boxer needs disciplined training and adequate recovery time to maintain both performance and long-term health.

words.definitionEn: an artificial waterway for boats or carrying water
words.exampleDailyEn: We watched a narrow boat glide along the canal.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Restoring historic canals can attract tourists while providing valuable habitats for wildlife in densely populated urban areas.

words.definitionEn: Someone whose job is repairing vehicles or machines.
words.exampleDailyEn: The mechanic found a leak under our car.
words.exampleIeltsEn: As electric vehicles become more common, mechanics need additional training to maintain their complex systems safely.

words.definitionEn: To repeat someone's exact words in speech or writing.
words.exampleDailyEn: My sister loves to quote lines from old films.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Students should quote reliable sources accurately and explain how the evidence supports their arguments in academic essays.

words.definitionEn: The function or responsibility someone or something has.
words.exampleDailyEn: My role is to welcome guests at the door.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public libraries play an important role in providing equal access to information and educational resources.

words.definitionEn: Able to be trusted to work well or behave consistently
words.exampleDailyEn: Our old car is still reliable in cold weather.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to reliable information helps citizens make informed decisions about their health and finances.

words.definitionEn: to be formed from particular parts or members
words.exampleDailyEn: Our picnic lunch consists of sandwiches, fruit, and juice.
words.exampleIeltsEn: An effective recycling programme consists of convenient collection services and clear guidance for local residents.

words.definitionEn: Something bought for less than its usual price
words.exampleDailyEn: This warm winter coat was a real bargain.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Consumers can often bargain with local sellers, although fixed prices are more common in large stores.

words.definitionEn: using science to design and build machines, structures, or systems
words.exampleDailyEn: My cousin studies engineering and builds small robots at home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Advances in engineering have enabled cities to build bridges that withstand extreme weather and carry heavier traffic.

words.definitionEn: An organised group of people who sing together.
words.exampleDailyEn: My sister sings in the choir every Sunday.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Joining a community choir can reduce loneliness and strengthen social connections among older adults.

words.definitionEn: finding something previously unknown, or the thing that is found
words.exampleDailyEn: We made an exciting discovery behind the old cupboard.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The discovery of new antibiotics could help health services respond more effectively to drug-resistant infections.

words.definitionEn: the habits and activities that shape how someone lives
words.exampleDailyEn: Cycling to work is part of her healthy lifestyle.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A sedentary lifestyle can increase health risks, particularly among people who spend long hours at desks.

words.definitionEn: in or near the middle of a place
words.exampleDailyEn: Our apartment is central, so we walk to most places.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to reliable information is central to helping citizens make informed decisions about public health.

words.definitionEn: An area of sea partly enclosed by land.
words.exampleDailyEn: Small fishing boats floated in the sheltered bay.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Coastal development around the bay must be carefully managed to protect marine habitats and local livelihoods.

words.definitionEn: A feeling of happiness or enjoyment
words.exampleDailyEn: She takes great pleasure in growing herbs on her balcony.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public libraries encourage reading for pleasure while providing affordable access to knowledge for people of all ages.

words.definitionEn: People watching or listening to a performance, speech, or programme
words.exampleDailyEn: The audience clapped loudly when the dancers finished.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Online platforms enable museums to reach a wider audience, including people who cannot visit their collections in person.
